reviews.text:
From a Yoga teacher in Training. I love this app. Makes it so easy to design classes and visualize flows. I also really like the option to include breath cues & holds. Also THRILLED that it’s stayed free for as long as I’ve had it, with no ads at all. There’s really nothing else out there like this. 

I am only giving this app 4 stars because I still think there is room for improvement. These are tiny little flaws/ suggestions within this otherwise awesome app:

• Occasional glitch where the picture of a pose will mirror the one next to it
• Glitch when linking with Spotify - I’ve only been able to successfully connect a song from Spotify one time, and it took multiple tries
• There’s no option to hold poses for less than 30 seconds. At least, it won’t let me adjust for less time than 30 seconds. Same thing with the breath timer. Many of my students aren’t up to a 6 second breath count yet (which is the shortest option)
• Why isn’t there an Apple Watch app for this? I know Pocket Yoga has an Apple Watch feature. I could DEFINITELY use the teacher version on my Watch
• Give us variations of poses! Give us more poses!
• Maybe make the “Custom Posture” feature a small symbol (like a triangle or something) instead of another yoga pose. Right now, it’s a cartoon of Awkward Pose. It would make more sense to simply have a small shape with space for a name instead of a cartoon of an actual yoga pose. 

As a side note, I think Pocket Yoga & Pocket Teacher should be integrated apps. You could maybe do free (and more limited) versions, but overall I know people would pay for an integrated version of these two awesome apps (especially if they had Apple Watch features for Pocket Teacher!)

Thanks for reading this lengthy review! Thanks for this awesome app!

I will come back to update to 5 stars if I see good changes.

Bravo. These folks designed a fine pair of Yoga applications. The drawings are simple and provide a clear picture of the asana. The voice is pleasant. The spoken instructions are well-timed, concise, clear, and instructive. I am sure I could say the same about any number of other Yoga applications. 

So what brings me to this rave review of 'Pocket Yoga Teacher?' I wanted to construct a series of poses in 'Pocket Yoga Teacher,' and it balked at doing them in the order I proposed. Suspecting a bug in the program, I contacted support and got a prompt reply from support. Let me repeat that. I GOT A PROMPT REPLY FROM SUPPORT. The folks supporting the application pointed out problems with the series of asanas I had in mind and offered improvements. The problem was an operator failure (me) and they corrected it.

These folks know a lot about Yoga and programmed it into their applications. It may not be blatantly obvious, but it was there lurking beneath the surface to help me.

Skip It. As a yoga instructor, I found this app to be inadequate for two reasons:

1.) The library of poses is really quite limited - app developers should not only offer primary poses, but their many variations, and they ought to be searchable by name (in both English and Sanskrit), which leads me to the next major issue...

2.) This app is in desperate need of a "Search" field. In my experience, searching poses within the app must be done manually - either by scrolling through alphabetical (English) pose names, or looking through the visual dictionary of pose tiles. While each pose is accompanied by it's Sanskrit name, the fact that there's no "Search" field means you have to scroll on, and on...to add a single pose. 

Was expecting a MUCH more comprehensive experience. Would not have purchased if I had this information.
Buy it. If you are an intermediate or advanced Yogi and dont want to spend that much time or money going to studios - buy it!

Yoga You Gonna Tailor!. Great user friendly apps! During my recovery from a brain surgery, I tailored a simple practice that wouldn't put pressure on my head and use it every day. I incrementally built up more poses and longer duration. Start off from 5 min practice, I m now at practice with more than 20 min and makes my body feels good and strong. Room for improvement to have more poses, music and audio cure options.

Addicted. I downloaded this app, and within three weeks I had built out 4 practices, tailored just for me! I've done yoga at least 4-5 times a week since, since it is so convenient and just the practice I need. With some years of amateur yoga under my belt, it was pretty easy to build these for myself. I look forward to working in some more challenging poses in the future...after all, I can hold the poses for as short or as long as I like, and build up to them with all the options available. Really great app, thank you! I hope others enjoy it, as well!

The app works well and exactly as advertised, so your practices are unique to you and thus are as meaningful and productive as you make them. I really do love this app!

Cons:
I bought several karma points so that I could get the Buddha background on my iPad. But the app forces you to buy them again on your iPhone despite both devices are the same account. Kind of cheap of them. That's a huge pet peeve of mine and always seems greedy of the developer.

2. Getting the music to voice thing worked out.

4. A way to save favorite sequences to quickly add them into a new routine.

1. The ability to create my own poses.

A month membership to a studio can cost over a hundred dollars! Here you can use your knowledge and practice on your own time to your own music.
Finally, I can enjoy my routine!. I've had a thorough routine that I had memorized for years, but when I'm rusty, It's no fun trying to remember all 20+ poses. This app takes the work out of it!!

Really great!. Overall loving it. Have a few suggestions for next version:
- Add names of poses to the images when building. I've often picked the wrong one (left instead of right, etc) because it's hard to see from the little image. 
- Allow to choose which VoiceOver you want - simple or basic. Sometimes she gives me the full instructions and sometimes just says name of pose, and I'm never sure why each are chosen. Allow us to choose. 
- Allow volume of music and VoiceOver be adjusted separately. 
- Maybe come preloaded with some typical routines, like Sun Salutation, to save the user some time. 

Overall really great though - love it!

Very easy to use, great for post-op personalized routine. I love this app! Super easy to use, nice interface. For an experienced yoga student (though not advanced), it's very easy to follow the routine I created. I am recovering from an operation and can't do most of a regular yoga class. With this app, I built myself a customized routine - so much more fun than my boring piece of paper with my physical therapy stretches!

Requests:
- add the option to insert a pose that is not in your list - allow me to type in & then see a brief text prompt as my cue for what to do
- add the standing quad stretch that is the preliminary pose for natarajasana
- make a version for physical therapy patients to use - standard PT exercises, customized by the therapist and downloaded to the patient's mobile device
Tai Chi Teacher. Great Yoga App! Love It!
Great trainer!. If you take the time to set up the kind of yoga practice you enjoy, you are going to love this app! Helps with instructor routines as well!
Too much fun. I am new to yoga but I can now take a routine with me no matter where I am.

Excellent, Couple of Suggestions. 1. Allow for adjusting volume of instructor and music...2 separate volume controls that can be adjusted while the practice is not in session.

2. Add plank pose

3. Add mountain pose without praying hands

4. Add pose explanations

5. Show pose names

6. For downward corpse pose, have 2 different ones: one looking left, the other looking right.

So easy to use!. Great app that makes it easy to create and follow routines between classes. I use this almost daily!

Awesome app!. I'm new to yoga so having the suggestions is great and u can set up everything and tailor it to your exact needs/boundaries

Great for the Office!. I am able to design a practice I can do in even the smallest of office space. It's a great way to stay healthy and active. Days I have to do a lot of sitting at the desk, I am still able to stretch and perform a practice I created.

At times all recommended poses were extremely awkward to follow the pose i selected and they also seemed to favor a few poses that i was not interested in.

OK, for free app. If you have done yoga, and understand how poses transition, and how to modify this may work for you. If you don't you might hurt yourself. Also PLEASE add a search function so I don't have to scroll endlessly to find a particular pose to add to the routine. Labels for poses would be nice too
Good. Goooooood

Great idea but still lacking.. I'm pretty into yoga so I was excited to try out this app. I think the concept is great, but I think it would be better to show the user how to get into it transition into these postures. I set up a small routine and all I saw was the woman go from one pose to another without actually moving her body into the pose, which is completely unrealistic. Another flaw IMO is that they don't show the names for the postures. I was trying to help someone new to yoga design a routine and walk him through via email which poses to do but couldn't. Having the actual names of each would've allowed me to do this. Crashed, lost routines. I love the concept and set up and did two routines set to some favorite tunes. Perfect for even a newbie. Love this app! I've created multiple practices for different days and even a 5 min one for at the office :-)

Great app. Great if you already know poses, but there is some coaching for poses. This app has really invigorated my practice.
Yoga app. Really enjoy this. Wish you could search poses. Sometimes it's hard to tell which leg is which and if there is a pose for both legs.
o b s e s s e d. I'm so bad at keeping to a routine when I do yoga. This app is awesome. I can organize my thoughts before I start without having to stop and read notes in the middle. I love it!

About what this app was from. I got this app from the starbucks app of the week and I did my my first single workout on Aug 23, 2012 for 34 minutes and 30 seconds. I was so excited! -Hayden LaCelle
History. Love this app! But could you add a history/ calendar so I can track how often I do my yoga a month? Thanks ?

Love it!. I really like this app, it definitely helps me to have a more regular home practice. Overall great app. As many have already said, this is a great app, and could be vastly better by
a few minor tweaks:
1. Categorize and Title the poses
2. Add feature to save sequences and then stitch together in a routine
3. Better pose descriptions and instructions
4. Add missing basic poses (cobblers, side bends)
5. Music/voice over volume adjustments
Great app. I like this as a newer yoga attendee I would like to see what others customized routines are to get a feeling for how long my routines should be

Great App!. I love creating my own routines visually! I cannot remember the names of all the moves and how they would go together smoothly. The visual, easy to create menu, is wonderful. I'm doing my stretches everyday now. Live it!

Great App, but please fix crashes. I love being able to create my own routines and this is a great App to do so. I think the built-in music is great too.

*** Please fix the crashes. It's frustrating to be editing your routine, have the app crash, and can't remember what you've removed/added/adjusted. ***

Wish list:

1. Be able to click Save, so as you edit, you can consciously save periodically.

2. Be able to save routine segments so I can join segments into routines. 

3. Have built-in Sun Salutation A and B segments available to add to routines. Users can end each customized segment with A or B, that way segment to segment will transition smoothly within any routine.

(Example: user creates segments 1, 2, 3... Then user can create a routine = segment 2 + Sun Salutation A + segment 1 + Sun Salutation B + segment 3 + Sun Salutation B...)

4. As suggested by another reviewer, note L or R on the pictures, because it's hard to tell which leg is forward by the thumbnails.

5. Echoing another reviewer, organize the poses into categories: Lounges, Standing, Back bends, etc.

6. Another echo, be able to save to Favorite Poses, so users can easily add poses from a shorter list.

Looking forward the updates. Great job thus far!

Effective. This app let's you create a highly customizable yoga sequence with audio and visual cues. It's great at what it does. I'd like to see the asanas sorted into categories and named. Also the ability to export the sequence as an audio file would be great.

Might be ok.... ...but I'm not all that interested in reading my way through two iPad screens full of teeny-tiny legal language to read what rights I'm signing away by using the application. Oh, and no way to print the agreement or store it so I can refer to it later. Clearly, the lawyers are the most important group at Rainfrog LLC -- not developers or users. Deleting.

Need setting options!!!!!!!. For a couple months now, I've been using the pocket yoga app and I've loved it. I was very excited when I finally decided to purchase this app. It's very easy to use, although it does glitch sometimes and crashes sometimes when I try to edit practices. These are things I can handle and didn't bother me too much but what REALLY frustrates me is that while I have my music set to play in the yoga practice, the voice of the instructor is much much MUCH louder! In the pocket yoga app at least there was a way to lower the volume of the voice but there's nothing like that in this. Also the meaning of "no audio cue" clearly doesn't mean there will be no audio cue since there is on one every asana!

Please fix the crashes and the audio settings in the next update because they're incredibly annoying.

Also a little diversity would be nice. Not that it really matters but it'd be cool to be able to pick different people from a different gender or ethnicity to do the asanas.

Including an option to have the actual Sanskrit names of the asanas would be nice too for those of us who want to learn them.

Almost there. Really cool app, easy and intuitive. I would like to suggest 2 things. First, when you're dealing with right or left leg poses, it's hard to tell which is which by the thumbnail. A small R or L in the thumbnail would alleviate the problem. Also, I would like to be able to have a 'my poses' section so I don't have to search through the (wonderfully) expansive set of poses when I'm repeating a sequence that lies outside of the suggested order of poses- maybe just be able to copy them over or highlight them somehow within the existing catalog. Overall though, really neat app.

This app is amazing. I wish there was a way to see the length of the music underneath your practice so you know when to add the next song. Otherwise, this app is wonderful. I'm really looking forward to the updates that will make this amazing app a perfect app. Definite download for any yogi.

I love this app!. This app is what I was looking for. I am very particular with yoga. I like certain timing, certain sequences, etc., etc., although other apps allow us to create our own programs, none is as easy, customizable, and enjoyable as this one. Having said that, if you know nothing about yoga, this is not the app for you as it offers no guidance.

Just a few tweaks. I love this app and the other app by the same developers.

However, I would like to point out a few things.

The poses are not categorized in any way, nor do they have their names by their icons. I would like to see the poses categorized into groups like lunges, forward bends, back bends, etc.

It seems the timer is incorrect when you set a duration of a pose in seconds. It goes by much too quickly.

I also ran into some issues while I was creating my sequence. When dragging a pose up and setting its duration, sometimes it would create a duplicate of itself or sometimes a totally new rendition if the same pose. I also ran into issues when placing the music onto it.

Also, I can't find a place to give an explanation of how to perform each pose. The pictures are good, and the VoiceOver sometimes gives an explanation, but I would like to see a description of how to perform each one as well as a list of pros, cons, etc. of each pose. 

Lastly, I cannot figure out how to save or name a sequence once finished.

Other than these aforementioned points, it's a VERY good app. There is a large variety of poses to choose from. It takes a while to get everything set up, but once you have it, it's fantastic! It's great for those who like to do their own thing rather than the same routine over and over. I say give I a try!

Yoga time. I like this app a lot. It leaves some things to be desired: the poses are not categorized, which would save a lot of time. There seems to be a lack of certain kinds of poses like twists, but a few complicated looking handstands ,which I dont think your average user would be messing around with anyway . The movie and music features are great, but to send a routine in this form, the receiver must also have the program. I think it will be great in designing my yoga classes to teach, but again, it is not exactly a time saver because of the non categorized poses.

NOT user friendly. This app is not for you if you want to be told how to do yoga. You are required to do everything for yourself and the instructions are terrible, hard to find/use and interpret. I've had no buggy problems and the interface is great.

reviews.text: Printouts way too small. I printed some sequences and find them way too small to be of any use. Much better product in this area is the yoga sequencing app by yoganista.ch

Functional but deceptive. Great app, love the ability to create so many sequences, variations of poses, integrate my Spotify playlists etc. 

BUT!~

One of the main selling points was creating custom sequences and SHARING them. 

It’s not until you dig through the FAQ’s to find that you cannot create your custom routines and share them into the normal Pocket Yoga app. This is weird... one app is called Pocket Yoga Teacher, and another Pocket Yoga advertised as for students/practitioners... 

It leads one to think, “well, I can create custom sequences and share them with my students” 

Except you can’t, unless they too download the Pocket Yoga Teacher app... Students should be able to access, download and play my custom routines, without the need to get the Teacher version of the app. Can someone explain why students should be expected to pay for the teacher version of the app, to perform basic functions provided in the main Pocket Yoga app? 

How much community can their really be if students have to pay for the teacher version of the app?

I’ve been on the teacher community for a year and it’s barely used... because nobody wants to pay $10+ to access their teachers routines!

I am not a teacher but this has helped me get a practice going by choosing poses and timing that works for me. 

I recommend this without reservations to teachers if you want to create new routines quickly.

An essential Asana class teacher resource. I have tried to adapt multiple sequence timers and workout builders on the App Store to enter and play my asana sequences. This one is clearly the best designed yoga sequence builder and it does feature an amazing number of poses to easily pick from and build your class. The layout and sharing capabilities are excellent.

Here are a few suggestions that would make this an indispensable resource for yoga teachers and sadhanas:

1) ability to add intervals between sequences required to safely get from one into the following pose. I suggest a global setting for the practice, and the ability to add custom breaks.

2) ability to set a half time reminder within pose, useful to change sides or make any other adjustment

3) a subtle near end-of-practice alert (choice of bells, hums, ...). The quality of the gong can be improved. A really quick (higher pitch) tone would be a great addition for those that just need a subtle hint to move into the next asana

4) choice of alerts (hums, bells) to optionally replace the voiceover. Support for Sanskrit voiceover, or at least ability to record your own would be much appreciated. Also, the voiceover does not include detail on which side (left or right) despite the ability to pick both

5) ability to set time (instead of breath) as default, and not having to redial 5 sec when setting minutes

6) the ability to import sequences into Pocket Yoga app. I thought that was what the bundle was all about
